mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a month indicates weakening labor market conditions, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate broader economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.05 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in real estate sales (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased consumer spending and confidence.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of periods with sustained HOUST increase, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a month indicates supply-side constraints, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face increased costs and reduced output.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it signals a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An interaction between a rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) and a falling real GDP (GDPC1) indicates stagflation, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL rises and GDPC1 falls in 1 quarter
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decreasing real GDP (GDPC1) over a quarter signals a tightening monetary policy in a slowing economy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings are squeezed.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and GDPC1 falls in 1 quarter
regime_hint: monetary tightening in a slowing economy
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in retail and food services sales (RSAFS) signals a strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as the broader economy benefits from increased consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 50% of periods with sustained RSAFS increase, or Rank IC < 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
